integrations.name: Optional mythic rival strategy planning
integrations.input: Encounter ID, Easy/Normal/Hard and at most two numeric attempt summaries. Server derives lane, timing and loss observations. No name, voice or chat text.
integrations.output: JSON with planId and focus. Each encounter permits two adaptive strategies. Server validates both and supplies the visible description.
integrations.timing: Use the October 8 six-call experiment. Preparation stops every game clock. Server timeout 90 seconds, browser limit 95 seconds.
integrations.privacy: Measured setup uses loopback Ollama. No third-party AI provider receives these requests. A hosted endpoint would receive the same numeric summary and needs a changed disclosure.
integrations.control: Edit difficulty/mode before play, cancel a pending call, regenerate a ready strategy, switch to Solo to reject it, or start a clearly labeled local AI duel after an error.

meta.title: Farshore
meta.subtitle: The Odyssey: Arcade Trials
meta.author: Bibek Pathak
meta.scope: A five-stop arcade voyage where each mythic rival uses a different game mechanic. Optional Llama planning chooses a legal rival strategy before a match.
meta.disclosure: Phase 2 designs document the current arcade prototype and explicitly labeled proposed controls. Maya, Daniel and Rosa are provisional Phase 1 persona sketches. Interview evidence and class peer critique have not been supplied.

personas.name: Maya, 21
personas.goal: Win through skill and understand why the rival behaves differently.
personas.need: Visible attack warnings, fixed scoring rules and a clear distinction between difficulty and rival strategy.
personas.evidence: The Phase 1 slide identifies a gamer concerned with fairness. These arcade design needs are hypotheses for evaluation, not interview findings.

personas.name: Daniel, 19
personas.goal: Experience the Odyssey without a confusing first encounter.
personas.need: One clear objective per shore, short practice, keyboard or touch controls and literary context.
personas.evidence: The Phase 1 slide identifies a reader with limited technical comfort. The arcade teaching flow is a proposed response to that sketch.

personas.name: Rosa, 34
personas.goal: Know what the model changes and keep control over its result.
personas.need: Model and local labels, visible strategy review, privacy disclosure, cancellation and a usable fallback.
personas.evidence: AI skepticism and the need for explanations come from the Phase 1 slide. No completed interview or AI trust score is asserted.

spike.method: Six sequential realistic samples using production POST adapter from a standalone script. No UI or game save. Raw provider outputs captured. Temperature 0, strict schema, 100 output-token cap, no streaming.
spike.scope: Feasibility and latency sample, not user research, enjoyment evidence, or a model accuracy benchmark.

answer.description: Noise heatmap. Polyphemus builds a noise heatmap and predicts the direction of your escape. A warning marks every smash before it lands.

messages.content: Prepare Polyphemus's policy. Output a JSON object with exactly planId and focus. Choose planId from focused or sweep. focus must be exactly "center", the game-derived habit. focused follows a heatmap of audible footsteps; sweep predicts the next grid position from the last two noise clues. The blind giant cannot see the player. Prefer focused for repeated losses, otherwise sweep. These policies execute locally after preparation. You cannot change speed, hit windows, scoring or progress. Return JSON only.

answer.description: Chain alchemist. Circe previews chain reactions or banks curses for a burst when your board is crowded.

messages.content: Prepare Circe's policy. Output a JSON object with exactly planId and focus. Choose planId from chain or hoard. focus must be exactly "balanced", the game-derived habit. chain previews the next potion for multi-chain matches; hoard uses the same planning but banks curses until the other board is crowded. Prefer chain for repeated losses, otherwise hoard. These policies execute locally after preparation. You cannot change speed, hit windows, scoring or progress. Return JSON only.

answer.description: Trick-note echo. The Sirens remember your missed lanes and weave those notes into the next melody. Trick rests and tempo changes are shown as they happen.

messages.content: Prepare The Sirens's policy. Output a JSON object with exactly planId and focus. Choose planId from swell or echo. focus must be exactly "balanced", the game-derived habit. swell repeats the weakest missed sound lane in new melodies; echo also adds visible rests and changes tempo between melodies. Choose a melody strategy using the missed-lane history. These policies execute locally after preparation. You cannot change speed, hit windows, scoring or progress. Return JSON only.

answer.description: Shield pincer. Scylla aims successive heads around your shield; Charybdis synchronizes the pull with incoming strikes.

messages.content: Prepare Scylla & Charybdis's policy. Output a JSON object with exactly planId and focus. Choose planId from pincer or undertow. focus must be exactly "balanced", the game-derived habit. pincer sends heads around the shield and synchronizes moderate whirlpool pull; undertow adds stronger synchronized pull during approaching attacks. Prefer pincer for repeated losses, otherwise undertow. These policies execute locally after preparation. You cannot change speed, hit windows, scoring or progress. Return JSON only.

answer.description: Block-shot gambit. Antinous calculates wind compensation and can choose a lower-scoring block shot to narrow your next opening.

messages.content: Prepare Antinous's policy. Output a JSON object with exactly planId and focus. Choose planId from surge or feint. focus must be exactly "balanced", the game-derived habit. surge calculates wind compensation for scored shots; feint can sacrifice rings to block and narrow the player's next ring opening. Prefer surge for repeated losses, otherwise feint. These policies execute locally after preparation. You cannot change speed, hit windows, scoring or progress. Return JSON only.

answer.description: Noise heatmap. Polyphemus builds a noise heatmap and predicts the direction of your escape. A warning marks every smash before it lands.

messages.content: Prepare Polyphemus's policy. Output a JSON object with exactly planId and focus. Choose planId from focused or sweep. focus must be exactly "left", the game-derived habit. focused follows a heatmap of audible footsteps; sweep predicts the next grid position from the last two noise clues. The blind giant cannot see the player. Prefer focused for repeated losses, otherwise sweep. These policies execute locally after preparation. You cannot change speed, hit windows, scoring or progress. Return JSON only.

quality: Legal focused/center. The prompt prefers sweep for a newcomer, but that preference is advisory. Selection is not proof of best tactics.
Legal chain/balanced. Matches the prompt preference for two previous losses. Rival still plays through local chain logic.
Legal echo/balanced. Red miss counts reach the prompt. Local melody logic targets the weakest lane; this output does not name red.
Legal pincer/balanced. Prompt favors undertow except for repeated losses, so this valid choice differs from its advisory preference.
Legal feint/balanced. Produces the block-shot policy. Whether the player finds it fair needs a playtest.
Legal focused/left. Required habit focus is preserved. This small result does not establish general adaptation quality.
